newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes inch lower in Asia, Oman firmer.
newsitem.headline: Crudes inch lower in Asia, Oman firmer.

text.p: Crude oil prices edged lower in Asia on Tuesday, extending overnight losses triggered by news that Iraq had agreed to all U.N. conditions on an oil-for-food deal, traders said. However, a trader said the Asian market was likely to respond cautiously to the step, which could lead to Iraq's return to the international oil market, because of past delays in implementing the deal. At Tokyo midday, January cash Brent was assessed at $22.60/22.70, down from late-Monday U.S. levels of $22.70/22.80. Brent/Dubai spreads narrowed on weaker Brent prices.
January was quoted at $1.85/1.95 compared with late U.S. trading levels of $1.95/2.00, and February was indicated at $1.85/1.93 compared with $1.85/1.95.
In Dubai spreads, January/February was assessed at 55/60 cents, and February/March at 46/50 cents.

In the wet market, Middle Eastern crudes largely remained firm in brisk trade, traders said. January Dubai changed hands at full-month quotes plus 80 cents between a Western trader and European oil firm, up a few cents from earlier deals.
Firm Dubai levels have also been adding to Oman's strength and boosting Oman's premiums, traders said.
